facts.text: FlexMotionController is a thin wrapper of OT3API: it reuses the OT3API implementation (CAN, calibration), provides a surface for motion, pipette and lights, and serialises hardware access through a lock shared with HardwareProxy

stop() is documented to halt all motion without waiting for the operation lock: it marks the recovery state halted, runs the OT3API halt() as a task and awaits it to completion; a cancellation that arrives meanwhile is re-raised only after the halt finished
mark_halted() increments the operation generation, requires a full robot home and cancels every active robot operation task other than the current one
operation_ready is false while a full re-home is required, and the operator guidance then begins with 'Fully re-home all robot axes'
_assert_operation_ready raises NotHomedError ('The robot is recovery-gated. ... before retrying.') when the recovery state is not operation-ready
A cancelled actuation registered by _active_operation marks the robot halted and awaits an OT3API halt() before its hardware lock is released; a failure of that halt is logged, not raised
home(axes=None) homes all axes; the operation-ready check runs only for a partial home (axes given), and a full home that no halt interrupted marks the robot fully homed
move_to(mount, point, speed=None) checks the recovery gate, validates the target, moves the mount to the absolute deck point and returns the gantry position read back after the move
The absolute-target validation rejects deck targets outside the transformed Flex machine-axis bounds of the OT3API backend
translate_motion_errors turns the OT3API PositionUnknownError and PositionEstimationInvalidError into NotHomedError and OutOfBoundsMove into MovementOutOfBoundsError
NotHomedError is documented as a move refused because the robot's position is unknown: home the robot before requesting a move
The connector's SiLA EmergencyStop runs FlexMotionController.stop() and states that a re-home is required before resuming
The connector's SiLA Home homes every axis and is documented as required after an emergency stop before further motion
The parity matrix names MotionControlFeature.EmergencyStop as the single pre-emptive, robot-wide halt path
set_lights(button=None, rails=None) sets the status-bar and/or deck lights under the operation lock; get_lights() returns the light state through the lock's observation view
The lock's observation view acquires the underlying lock with acquire() unless that lock offers acquire_observation, waiting at most the lock's timeout_s
machine_status() reads the cached E-stop state, the door state and the derived error flag without CAN I/O or the operation lock
is_simulating reports whether the underlying OT3API is a simulator backend
build() makes a standalone controller with its own OT3API and lock: simulate=True builds the OT3API hardware simulator, simulate=False the real CAN hardware controller
disconnect() releases the hardware resources of a standalone controller by calling the OT3API clean_up() under the operation lock
The README says one shared OT3API serialises the SiLA and HTTP servers so their CAN commands cannot interleave, and avoids the 'hardware already initialised' error two separate processes would hit
The README says the standard opentrons-robot-server service is disabled on deployment and the sila2-connector service owns the hardware
Motion is exposed per mount (LEFT, RIGHT, GRIPPER) in deck coordinates (x, y, z mm), matching the Flex hardware API
The operator preparation checklist says to close the door, disengage the E-stop, clear all travel corridors and keep the E-stop reachable

safe_state.description: FlexMotionController.stop() has cancelled the registered in-flight operation and awaited the OT3API halt(), and the connector refuses every actuation except a full home (the declared re-enable) until one completes; nothing senses motor standstill, and whether the motors stay energised or hold position after the halt is not stated in the clone (OT3API is outside it)
